note: Research conferences and calls for abstracts that fit SafeSmoke Carbon and Carbon Clarity: clean cooking and stoves, carbon markets and climate finance, fisheries and coastal communities, gender and just transitions. Checked on the official pages; dates can change, so confirm before submitting.

items.name: International Conference on Climate Change and Just Energy Transition (I3C-JET 2027)
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts by 31 March 2027, 17:00 GMT, to i3c-jet@wascal.org. Call opened 15 November 2026.
items.fee: Africa and low/middle-income countries US$150; Master's/PhD students US$50; online US$30
items.fit: Best fit. West African, and its themes include carbon sequestration and blue/green carbon finance, economics and climate finance, low-carbon development and just energy transition, marine sciences and blue economy, and migration.
items.angle: SafeSmoke Carbon: measured fuel savings and portable benefit sharing for women fish smokers in displaced and host communities.

items.name: ETHOS 2027: the clean cookstove conference
items.deadlineNote: The listing invites submissions but gives no deadline. Check the ETHOS site now: the conference is in early February.
items.fit: The main meeting for stove testing and cookstove carbon. Opens with 'Carbon 101' and 'Stoves 101' training on 4 February. The virtual option makes it affordable.
items.angle: Measuring kg of wood per kg of fish: a sensor protocol for commercial fish-smoking kilns.

items.name: 2027 Energy and Climate Economics and Business Days
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts or panel proposals by 15 January 2027; decisions 25 January; presenter registration by 26 February.
items.fee: €125 (both days, with meals); travel not covered
items.fit: Energy transition and climate change economics, broadly defined, including empirical work. A short abstract is enough.
items.angle: Who gets paid? Benefit-sharing design for clean-cooking carbon credits in Ghana.

items.name: EAERE 2027: European Association of Environmental and Resource Economists annual conference
items.deadlineNote: Papers, science-policy-business and thematic session proposals by 31 January 2027. Participation grant applications by 10 February 2027.
items.fit: Top environmental economics meeting. Needs a full paper, so it suits your Ghana carbon market research once written up.
items.angle: Ghana's Article 6 carbon market: who benefits? (from your research report)

items.name: SER2027: 12th World Conference on Ecological Restoration
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts (talks, lightning talks, posters) open 3 December 2026 and are due 29 January 2027.
items.fee: Not yet published; early bird from 14 January 2027
items.fit: Fits the mangrove side of SafeSmoke: fish smokers burn mangrove wood (Keta), and your community fund can pay for replanting. Has a finance and socioeconomic impact series.
items.angle: Cutting mangrove fuelwood demand through cleaner fish smoking in Ghana.

items.name: ECAS 2027: 11th European Conference on African Studies, 'African Prisms'
items.deadlineNote: The call for panels closed 27 September 2026. Papers are submitted to accepted panels; watch for the call for papers.
items.fit: Large African studies meeting with panels on environment, gender and livelihoods. Look for a panel on climate, fisheries or carbon.
items.angle: Women, smoke and carbon: fish processors and Ghana's carbon market.

items.name: Innovate4Climate 2027
items.deadlineNote: Registration details to come on the official site.
items.fit: The World Bank's flagship meeting on carbon pricing and carbon markets: buyers, developers and governments, including Article 6 deals.
items.angle: Networking: meet buyers and developers for a pilot of SafeSmoke credits.

items.name: ISEE 2027 Biennial Conference (International Society for Ecological Economics)
items.deadlineNote: Submission dates not yet published; the conference awaits final authorisation.
items.fit: Ecological economics, global South themes and just transitions.
items.angle: Fair carbon: activity rights instead of land rights for mobile women workers.

items.name: What Works Climate Solutions Summit 2027
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts closed 20 September 2026. Travel support 'under development': ask info@wwcs.science.
items.fit: Evidence on climate solutions in the global South, including food systems and health.
items.angle: Attend; plan an abstract for the next edition.

items.name: Second Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa
items.organiser: IEA, co-chaired by Kenya, Norway and the United States, with the African Union and AfDB
items.deadlineNote: The IEA says governments, institutions and companies have been invited; no public registration or call for proposals is published. Watch the IEA event page and ask partners (e.g. Clean Cooking Alliance, Ghana Energy Commission) about side events or livestream.
items.fit: The top policy and finance meeting for clean cooking in Africa (over USD 900 million in new commitments already). Directly relevant to SafeSmoke's kiln, cookstove carbon credits and finance for women processors.
items.angle: Share a one-page brief: productive-use clean cooking (fish-smoking kilns) as a missing category in Africa's clean cooking finance, with sensor-verified wood savings.

items.name: CSAE Conference 2027: Economic Development in Africa
items.organiser: Centre for the Study of African Economies, University of Oxford
items.deadlineNote: The call for papers has closed. Registration is open: speaker deadline 4 January 2027, general deadline 21 February 2027.
items.fee: Not stated on the conference page (registration via Cvent)
items.support: Limited funding for African presenters living and working in Africa (presenters only; requires a pre-conference workshop in late 2026)
items.fit: The leading meeting on African development economics; a place to meet economists working on energy, environment and markets in Ghana and West Africa. Note the 2028 call for papers for future work on Ghana's carbon market.
items.angle: For a future call: who gains from Ghana's carbon credits? Benefit-sharing rules under the Carbon Market Office and effects on women fish processors.

items.name: Conference on Advancing Africa's Industrialisation: Regional Value Chains for a Green and Resilient Future (AfCFTA Conference 2027)
items.organiser: Nelson Mandela School of Public Governance, University of Cape Town
items.deadlineNote: Full papers, policy briefs, case studies or panel proposals by 31 January 2027. Contact: mapoulo.ntoane@uct.ac.za.
items.fit: African green industrialisation, climate finance and a 'Towards COP32' session. SafeSmoke is a green value-chain upgrade for fish processing, a strong policy-brief angle.
items.angle: Greening Africa's fish value chain: cleaner kilns, measured fuel savings and carbon income for women processors (policy brief or case study).

items.name: EGU General Assembly 2027 (European Geosciences Union)
items.deadlineNote: The call for abstracts is open; check the exact abstract and financial-support deadlines on the EGU27 'Deadlines and milestones' page. Session ERE0.1 'Bridging the gap between climate risk and energy access' fits SafeSmoke.
items.fee: Not stated here; EGU offers fee waivers and financial support (check eligibility)
items.support: Financial support and waivers (check the EGU27 page)
items.fit: Huge hybrid meeting with an online option. The energy-access and climate-risk session matches clean fish-smoking energy and measured savings.
items.angle: Measuring energy access at the kiln: sensor evidence of fuel savings in Ghana's fish smoking.

items.name: Environmental Markets Conference 2027
items.organiser: Alliance for Environmental Markets and Investments (AEMI)
items.deadlineNote: The main call has closed; digital presentations and posters are open until 5 March 2027.
items.support: Financial assistance and awards page (check eligibility)
items.fit: Has a 'Carbon Markets & Climate Solutions' track covering MRV, voluntary markets and climate finance. Good for networking with credit buyers, but travel to the USA is costly.
items.angle: Poster: digital MRV and fair benefit sharing for small-scale clean-cooking credits in Ghana.
